sentence: A routine GP appointment is the usual route if joint pain, rashes or extreme tiredness keep coming back, since lupus is easier to manage when found early.

sentence: Seizures, new weakness, vision problems or chest pain on deep breathing call for prompt medical assessment: NHS 111 or the GP the same day, and call 999 if they are severe or sudden.

sentence: Lupus symptoms vary widely from person to person and can come and go.

sentence: The NHS lists joint and muscle pain and extreme tiredness that does not go away however much a person rests as main symptoms.
A rash often appears across the nose and cheeks and can get worse in sunlight.
NIAMS describes this as a butterfly-shaped rash.
note: NIAMS: butterfly-shaped rash across cheeks and nose.

sentence: Other possible signs include headaches, mouth ulcers, fever, hair loss, weight loss and swollen glands.
Some people have Raynaud's, where the fingers and toes change colour.
note: NHS: Raynaud's (colour changes in fingers and toes).

sentence: Arthritis in lupus can cause painful, swollen joints and morning stiffness.
Lupus can also affect organs such as the kidneys, heart, lungs and brain.
Early symptoms can be mistaken for another type of inflammatory arthritis and may appear months or years before a diagnosis.
Lupus is an autoimmune condition, which means the immune system attacks healthy tissue.
It is not contagious.
The exact trigger is unclear, but the NHS lists possible contributors including viral infections, certain medicines, sunlight, puberty, childbirth and the menopause.
Unusual antibodies that react against the body's own tissue are found in the blood, and the resulting inflammation can damage tissues.
note: Search summary: SLE marked by unusual autoantibodies; immune complex deposition drives chronic inflammation and tissue damage. Page attribution blended.

sentence: Lupus is more common in women, and the NHS says it is more common in people of African, Caribbean, Asian or Chinese background.

note: City and Hackney guideline: SLE is rare.

sentence: Because the symptoms overlap with other conditions, diagnosis can take time.
No single test confirms lupus, and doctors combine the person's history, a physical examination and laboratory tests.
Symptoms also change over time, so lupus can be misdiagnosed.
note: Search summary: symptoms change over time, so misdiagnosis is common.

sentence: A GP usually starts with blood tests.
The ANA test is often the first step, but a positive result alone does not confirm lupus because healthy people can also test positive.
Doctors may also order blood counts, kidney function tests and urine protein checks, and sometimes a tissue biopsy.
Imaging of the heart, kidneys or other organs may follow if they seem to be affected.
The NHS says lupus may be diagnosed if tests show a high level of a certain type of antibody and the person also has the typical symptoms.
There is no cure for lupus, but the NHS says symptoms can improve if treatment starts early.
NIAMS says care is tailored to symptoms and aims to manage them and to prevent, limit and stop flares.
Options named by the NHS include anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen, hydroxychloroquine for fatigue, skin and joint problems, and steroids for kidney inflammation and rashes.
For severe cases, immunosuppressant or biological medicines may be used.
note: NHS; NIAMS lists immunosuppressants and newer biologics.

sentence: NIAMS says doctors generally use corticosteroids at the lowest effective dose because of their side effects.
Severe involvement of the heart, lungs, kidneys and other organs often needs specialist care.
NIAMS stresses that medicines should not be stopped without medical advice.
note: NIAMS living-with-lupus summary: not stopping medication without medical advice.

sentence: Flares, when symptoms worsen, range from mild to serious and do not follow a pattern.
note: NIAMS: flares mild to serious, no pattern.

sentence: Lupus UK describes a flare as a time when the disease becomes active and symptoms worsen or new ones appear, with quieter periods in between.
note: Lupus UK summary: flares alternate with remission.

sentence: NIAMS says learning a person's own warning signs helps, and that many people with lupus live satisfying and productive lives.
The NHS self-care advice includes sun protection, pacing yourself, staying active and managing stress.
Sun protection includes a high-factor sunscreen and a hat.
note: Search summary of NHS guidance: high-factor sunscreen plus a hat.

sentence: Other advice includes not smoking and eating a balanced diet with vitamin D and calcium.

sentence: Regular visits to the doctor are emphasised.

sentence: Severity varies, and a severe case can cause serious inflammation of the heart, lungs, brain or kidneys.

Kidney involvement often gives no symptoms, so it is found through urine and blood tests.
Lupus UK says an increased risk of miscarriage is a complication of lupus, and that many women with lupus have healthy pregnancies when planned.

sentence: Serious pregnancy complications such as pre-eclampsia and premature birth are more likely when lupus is active in early pregnancy.
